A customs union led by Prussia, in force from 1 January 1834, that removed tariffs between its members; Austria was not a member.

front: What did the Carlsbad Decrees (1819) do?
back: Censored the press, banned the Burschenschaften, put universities under curators and set up an investigating commission at Mainz.
A May 1832 gathering of tens of thousands in the Bavarian Palatinate that demanded freedom and German unity.

front: What were the Six and Ten Articles of 1832?
back: Repressive measures that strengthened princes against their assemblies and banned political associations, meetings and national symbols.

Why did liberals and nationalists often work together before 1848?
back: Both wanted an end to princely absolutism and censorship; liberals sought constitutions, nationalists sought a united state, and the Confederation resisted both.

front: Why did the crisis of 1846-47 matter?
back: Harvest failure, high food prices and an industrial slump brought distress to workers and artisans, who then joined the middle class in political protest.

front: What were the strengths of the German Confederation?
back: It protected the states from French attack, kept Austria and Prussia cooperating, and preserved peace between German states for decades.
